jobs.description: Employer: ENFOS Inc. Expires: 11/08/2026 ENFOS is redefining how global enterprises manage long-term environmental risk. As the category leader in Environmental Obligation Management, our platform centralizes and automates the full lifecycle of Environmental Remediation Obligations (EROs) and Asset Retirement Obligations (AROs)—replacing fragmented spreadsheets and outdated tools with a purpose-built, multi-tenant SaaS platform.For 25 years, ENFOS has helped the world’s leading industrial companies stay audit-ready, SOX-compliant, and financially in control of their environmental obligations. Privately held and profitable, ENFOS operates with no direct competitors and supports a blue-chip customer base spanning energy and natural resources, chemicals, manufacturing, and logistics end markets.With regulatory pressure rising and ESG scrutiny intensifying, ENFOS is uniquely positioned to empower Finance, Legal, and Remediation teams to improve decision-making, mitigate risk, and drive long-term balance sheet reliability. As an intern, you’ll work alongside experienced SCS professionals on projects encompassing comprehensive application of civil engineering principles (i.e., site development, drainage, soil mechanics, fluid mechanics, etc.) with emphasis on solid waste facilities such as landfills, transfer stations, material recovery facilities, and renewable natural gas plants. jobs.title: Building Enclosure Engineering Intern/Co-op - Summer '27 at RDH Building Science
jobs.description: Employer: RDH Building Science Expires: 11/08/2026 We are currently accepting applicants for our Summer 2027 Intern/Co-ops in the following offices: Seattle, WA; Portland, OR; Oakland, CA; Los Angeles, CA; and Boston, MA. Please specify which location(s) you're interested in in the appropriate field on your application.Note - these are full-time, in-person Internships/Co-ops and are not available for part-time or remote work._________________Do you have a passion for Making Buildings Better? If so, we want to hear from you!RDH is an employee-owned consulting firm with 300+ employees in 10 offices across North America. Our core area of business is the integration of building science engineering, architecture, and construction management to optimize the performance of the building enclosure (walls, windows and roofs). Since our beginnings in 1997, we have become industry leaders in North America and continue to grow as we focus on technical excellence and delivering high-quality projects. We approach projects with a multi-faceted and distinctly advanced understanding of building enclosures. We are grounded by our core values: 1) commit to excellence, 2) act with integrity, 3) work as a team 4) do what it takes, and 5) always learn.Our areas of work include collaborating with design teams for new building construction projects, forensic investigation and renewal of existing buildings, building asset management to assist building owners with the long-term upkeep and efficient use of their facilities, and building science research to identify ways of improving building stock.We hire enthusiastic engineering students who have basic training in building science engineering (building science, civil engineering, structural engineering, mechanical engineering, or architecture), along with exposure to hands-on experience in construction. We value innovative thinking, a passion for the field, and a strong sense of teamwork.Key ResponsibilitiesAs an engineering co-op student at RDH, you will work directly with senior staff on a variety of projects. Tasks and responsibilities will include:Field review of building enclosure components for new construction and renewal projects.On-site performance testing of building enclosure assemblies, including air leakage and window water testing.Investigation of existing buildings, including visual review of as built conditions, documenting conditions via field notes, sketches, and photos, and providing recommendations for repair, renewal or rehabilitation.Design and implementation of building asset management programs.Research and testing in our in-house lab for new technologies and strategies for reducing energy consumption, optimizing resources, and improving durability of buildings. Career Development and Training:During your work term, you will be mentored by a variety of staff from senior to junior, many of whom are industry leaders in building science engineering, architecture, and project management.We strive to develop students to become leading engineers in the building science space. We offer regular in-house continuing education seminars on a variety of technical topics, such as through our Building Science Live webinar series and regional Lunch and Learns. You may also attend external professional development events. By the end of the work term, we expect you will:Develop skills in building enclosure investigation, field review and design.Develop engineering problem solving skills related to building science.Learn how to perform field quality assurance that conforms to ASTM standards, including water testing of windows.Learn to assess water ingress and other building performance related problems.Learn about construction material performance characteristics using various software programs and confirmation in the field.Compensation & PerksThe base salary range for this position is $46,000-$64,000 annualized for a full-time role. Salary is dependent various factors, including qualifications, skills, competencies, experience, and location. You may also be eligible for relocation allowance, transportation expense coverage, paid vacation and paid sick leave.RDH will assist students with travel expenses and can provide information on housing options. Through our green transportation policy, we assist all employees with public transportation expenses.

jobs.title: Design Technology Interns (AutoCAD, Revit & 3D Modeling) at Haworth
jobs.description: Employer: Haworth Expires: 11/09/2026 Job Title: Design Technology Interns (AutoCAD, Revit & 3D Modeling)Company Overview At Haworth, we're not just creating office furniture; we're shaping dynamic workspaces. As a global leader in workspace solutions, we're on a journey to redefine the future of work. Headquartered in Holland, Michigan, Haworth is a family-owned global powerhouse at the forefront of innovation and sustainable design in the workspace interiors industry. Here, you'll get hands-on with state-of-the-art resources, interact with cross-functional teams of passionate innovators, and experience a blend of global reach and family-owned feel. Whether you're developing new manufacturing processes, implementing smart factory solutions, or designing tomorrow's workspace solutions, you'll be empowered to make a lasting impact. We are currently looking for a three paid interns to join our Design Technology team in Holland, MI. These positions will work onsite at the Haworth Corporate Headquarters. AutoCAD Intern Job Overview: As an AutoCAD Intern, you will create and optimize the 2D and 3D product symbols used by designers to specify and purchase Haworth products. You will learn the symbol creation process, develop and maintain CAD-based product symbols and reusable digital content standards, and help establish graphic-count standards that ensure products are detailed enough for photorealistic renderings while remaining lightweight enough to support complex floor plans. You will also analyze existing symbol libraries, document best practices and standards, and help create guidance that drives consistency across all product symbols. As part of the team's continuous improvement efforts, you will have the opportunity to explore AI and automation solutions to streamline symbol creation processes and support large-scale updates across the symbol library. 3D Modeling Intern Job Overview: As a 3D Modeling Intern, you will transform scans, product data, and reference materials into high-quality digital assets used across Haworth's visualization platforms. Working with 3D scans, engineering documentation, and photo references, you will develop high-quality 3D product models that balance visual realism with the performance requirements needed for large floor plan layouts. You will assist in troubleshooting and improving 3D scanning processes, transforming captured scan data into usable 3D assets, and applying textures and materials to create polished, production-ready symbols. In addition, you will help manage and release product cross-reference data using Excel, ensuring accuracy and a seamless user experience. Throughout the internship, you will also collaborate with cross-functional teams to interpret inconsistent data, validate information, document assumptions, and contribute to ongoing process and data quality improvements. Revit Intern Job Overview: As a Revit Intern, you will develop Building Information Modeling (BIM) content that helps architects, designers, and dealers visualize and specify Haworth products within Revit. You will create and update Revit families for Haworth products, building accurate 2D and 3D geometry from product drawings, CAD files, dimensions, and other reference materials. You will add and validate parameters, materials, visibility settings, and product information to ensure content performs effectively within real-world design projects. You will also test and troubleshoot Revit families for accuracy, usability, graphic quality, and file performance while supporting quality reviews and enhancements to Haworth's existing Revit content library. In addition, you will help document best practices and standardized development processes, gaining exposure to product development through collaboration with design, engineering, marketing, and Revit team members. Your work will directly contribute to the digital tools customers use to visualize, plan, and specify Haworth products in commercial spaces. Get ready for an adventurous summer as a Haworth intern! You'll join a cohort of around 50 other dynamic interns for a 12-week program packed with meaningful projects and weekly learning opportunities. You’ll attend NeoCon, the largest commercial design event in the world, where you will get an insider's look at all the latest industry trends and innovations. Sharpen your skills with interactive workshops on networking, public speaking, and using AI tools in a business environment. Connect with mentors and see all areas of the office and manufacturing processes. Then unwind at intern-only social events where you can meet people from all corners of the business. By the end of the summer, you'll leave with real skills, an expanded professional network, and memories to last a lifetime. This is your chance to take your career to new heights! Required Qualifications Full-time college enrollment, working towards a Bachelor’s Degree in Design Technology, Interior Design, Industrial Design, Architecture, Engineering Technology, Digital Design, or related field with at least a junior level status by Fall of 2027. Ability to work onsite in Holland, MI from May 2027 to August 2027. Applicants must possess an unrestricted right to work in the US to be eligible for the position. Preferred Qualifications A portfolio demonstrating coursework, internships, personal projects, or professional work related to interior design, architecture, product design, visualization, or digital content creation is preferred.Overall GPA of 2.95 or higherPrior Haworth experienceExperience with design and drafting software such as AutoCAD, Autodesk Revit, and SketchUpExperience with Blender, 3ds Max, or comparable 3D modeling and visualization software.Previous Employment experienceExtra-curricular activity experience such as athletics, clubs, volunteer work, etc. Ideally, you have also demonstrated the following: Ability to manage assigned projects to completion.Strong attention to detail.Working knowledge of business software applications, including Microsoft Excel.Desire to learn, question, and research solutions to problems. Organized with the ability to manage deadlines. Effective verbal and written communication skills.

jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/09/2026 Application Deadline 11/9/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription *Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.CDC Office and Location: A research opportunity is available in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), located in Atlanta, Georgia.The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is one of the major operation components of the Department of Health and Human Services. CDC protects America from health, safety and security threats, both foreign and in the U.S. Whether diseases start at home or abroad, are chronic or acute, curable or preventable, human error or deliberate attack, CDC fights disease and supports communities and citizens to do the same. CDC increases the health security of our nation. As the nation’s health protection agency, CDC saves lives and protects people from health threats. To accomplish its mission, CDC conducts important science and provides health information that protects our nation against expensive and dangerous health threats, and responds when these arise.The Acquisitions and Information Technology Solutions Activity (AITSA) is located in the Office of the Director within the Global Immunization Division (GID) of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, Georgia. The mission of AITSA is to deliver robust GID IT solutions, manage the Division-wide Interagency Agreements (IAA) portfolio, and oversee contracts for the GID Office of the Director (OD). We strive for excellence by providing efficient, effective technological support, fostering collaboration across the Division, and ensuring the success of GID's mission through innovative solutions and reliable partnerships.Research Project: You will engage in an applied learning and research project within AITSA in CDC’s GID. The project will examine how information technology, data analytics, automation, visualization, and emerging technologies can be applied to improve the accessibility, organization, analysis, and use of information supporting global immunization program activities.You may train on projects involving Power BI reporting and dashboards, data management and visualization, SharePoint site development, Microsoft 365 Solutions, Power Platform tools, workflow automation, and the exploration of responsible AI applications for public health. In addition, you may learn how IT projects are designed and supported by observing requirement-gathering practices and gaining experience contributing to educational materials such as user guides, job aids, and technical documentation under mentor guidance. Learning Objectives: You will have opportunities to strengthen skills while gaining exposure to enterprise IT within CDC's GID. Under the guidance of a mentor you will:Develop knowledge of public health information technology by learning how enterprise IT, data, and digital tools are used to support CDC global immunization programs.Strengthen data analytics and visualization skills through guided experience exploring datasets and developing reports, visualizations, and dashboards using tools such as Microsoft Power BI.Gain experience with data management practices, including organizing, validating, transforming, documenting, and presenting information for programmatic use.Develop skills with Microsoft 365 and collaborative technologies, including learning how SharePoint and related tools can support information sharing, knowledge management, and collaboration.Explore low-code/no-code development and workflow automation using Microsoft Power Platform and related technologies to understand how routine processes may be streamlined or improved.Explore responsible applications of artificial intelligence by examining potential AI-enabled approaches relevant to information management, analysis, automation, or other public health use cases while considering appropriate limitations and responsible-use practices.Learn requirements-analysis methodologies by observing and participating in structured approaches for gathering, documenting, validating, and translating stakeholder needs into potential technical solutions.Develop experience evaluating technology solutions by comparing potential approaches, documenting findings, participating in testing or prototype development, and considering usability and implementation requirements.Strengthen technical communication and documentation skills through collaborationon preparation of research summaries, process documentation, user guides, job aids, presentations, and other technical materials.Strengthen professional collaboration and communication skills through interaction with multidisciplinary staff and presentation of project findings and lessons learned to mentors and relevant GID stakeholders.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Marques Adams (msa9@cdc.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: October 30, 2026. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year, but may be renewed upon recommendation of CDC and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and CDC. Participants do not become employees of CDC, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility.Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process please email CDCrpp@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.Qualifications The qualified candidate should be currently pursuing or have received an associate's, bachelor's, or master's degree in the one of the relevant fields (e.g. Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, Computer Systems, Cybersecurity, or another closely related technical or computational field).Preferred skills:Interested in applying technology and data-driven solutions to real-world organizational and public health challenges.Prior experience in public health.An interest in learning how information technology, data, and emerging technologies can support public health programs is highly desirable.Outstanding critical thinking and problem-solving skills, as well as strong oral and written communication abilities.Stipend $5,439.00 – $6,581.00 MonthlyPoint of Contact RachelEligibility Requirements Citizenship: U.S. Citizen OnlyDegree: Associate's Degree, Bachelor's Degree, or Master's Degree.Minimum Overall GPA: 3.30

jobs.title: Visuals Systems and AI Design Intern at The Autoimmune Fund
jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 11/09/2026 About The Autoimmune FundAutoimmune and immune-mediated diseases affect millions of people, most of them women. Yet the money has gone almost entirely one way. Of the $40.0 billion in venture funding that went to the field from 2014 to 2025, 94.4% went to drug therapeutics. Prediction, diagnostics, devices, care access, monitoring and remission maintenance shared the remaining 5.6%. The Autoimmune Fund, a seed and Series A venture fund dedicated exclusively to autoimmune and immune-mediated disease, exists to back the rest.We invest across the whole spectrum of care. We lead investments everywhere except drug therapeutics, where we co-invest. Our thesis follows three scientific revolutions reshaping the field: Immune Precision, Accelerated Aging, and Female Biology.We are a small team that runs on AI. Everything we publish, from The Autoimmune Decade, our annual report launching in January 2027, to our slides, one-pagers and infographics, runs on one visual system. We want that system to be precise enough that an AI can apply it as reliably as a trained designer. What You'll DoYou will own how the fund looks, and teach an AI to hold that standard.First project: align our visual communication system. Audit our palette, typography, icons, chart styles, grids and layout rules across documents and slides. Find where they conflict, propose the rulings, and turn the result into one clear, written source of truth with components ready to use.Second project: train Claude on our design system. Set up our brand inside Claude's design tools (Claude Design) and write the instructions and reusable skills that teach it our rules. Generate slides, one-pagers and infographics, compare them against the standard, find where the AI drifts, and fix the instructions until it stops.Then: extend the system as the fund grows. Carry the system and its AI workflows into new formats, including report exhibits, social posts and web pages, so every piece we publish looks like it came from one hand. You HaveCurrent enrollment in an undergraduate program in design, visual communication, HCI, or a related fieldA portfolio that shows at least one system, such as a brand identity, type system or component library, not only single piecesReal typographic judgment: pairing, hierarchy, grids, and setting numbers so they alignDiscipline with a constrained palette, including contrast and accessibilityAdvanced Figma: components, styles and variables, not just drawingReal, hands-on AI use. You've built prompts, custom instructions, projects or workflows in tools like Claude or ChatGPT, and you can show us oneClear writing. Training an AI is mostly turning taste into precise, testable rulesAvailability to work in person in Los Angeles Nice to HaveCoursework or lab experience in immunology, biology or another life scienceData visualization experienceBasic HTML/CSS or MarkdownInterest in healthcare, biotech or venture capital What You'll GetDirect mentorship. You work side by side with the fund's Managing Partner, a clinician and former Wall Street healthcare equity analyst who covered 500+ companies over 14 years.Work that ships. What you build goes into real investor materials and our annual report, not a drawer.Builder-level AI skills. You will design, test and fix AI systems, not just prompt them.A front-row seat to venture. See how a specialist fund sources companies, weighs science and makes decisions.A portfolio piece few undergrads have. A working design system and the AI that applies it, both built by you. To ApplySend your resume, a portfolio with at least one system project, and a short note (200 words max) describing one design rule you once had to make precise enough for someone else to follow, and what went wrong the first time to bonnie@autoimmune.fund. Work Test (3 to 4 hours, unpaid)We'll send you a packet: an excerpt of our brand rules, three past pieces of ours, and two pages of raw content (Content A and Content B). Send everything back as one PDF plus your instruction file. Unfinished parts are fine if you tell us what you would do next.1. Rule the conflicts. Our rules and our past pieces do not fully agree. List every conflict you find. For each, state the rule you would adopt and why, in one sentence. Flag anything else in the packet you think is wrong.2. Design the standard. Design a one-pager from Content A in Figma or a similar tool, by hand, with no AI-generated imagery. This is the reference the AI must match.3. Teach the AI. Write one set of instructions (a skill, custom instructions or a system prompt) that gets an AI to produce Content B in the same system. The same instructions must work on both pages. No hand edits to the AI output.4. Score it. Write at least ten pass/fail checks for this system. Score your AI output against them. An honest 7 out of 10 beats an inflated 10 out of 10.5. Show the work. Share the full chat log. In 150 words or fewer, tell us where the AI failed and what that taught you about writing instructions.

jobs.description: Employer: Man Group Expires: 11/10/2026 The TeamMan Systematics’ Fast Trading Strategies (FTS) team is responsible for the development of high Sharpe, high-frequency trading strategies across all asset classes. The team has been running for over a decade and currently manages a large and successful portfolio across both global futures and cash markets. The FTS team is responsible for the full end to end development of the fast alpha portfolio, using several techniques to capture fast alphas, ML, event driven, microstructure based etc, building its own customized monetization stack, and optimizing trading and order placement with dedicated high-frequency infrastructure.This posting is specifically for candidates interested in interning in the New York office, which houses Man Systematics’ business unit focused on high-frequency alpha research, trading, and infrastructure.Who Should Apply?The team is currently hiring PhD students for an MLE/QR internship with strong academic achievement in highly technical degree programs who are interested in a summer internship (expected to be between 10 – 12 weeks).Candidates are encouraged to submit only one application using their university email address via the below link, which requires a resume that includes all completed and in-progress post-secondary education GPAs. School transcripts may be optionally provided immediately or later in the process.Kindly note that our summer internships are open to penultimate year students only.Purpose of the RoleThe MLE role is ideal for individuals who are passionate about software that is focused on machine learning applications such as MLOps and research workflows. Because MLEs are also expected to use their own software, the ideal candidate not only has experience coding in a variety of languages (especially Python) but also has knowledge of ML algorithms and research processes.The QR role is ideal for individuals who are passionate about using high frequency tick data and machine learning algorithms to predict asset returns and converting those models into profitable trading strategies. QRs will work closely with MLOps in deploying models and therefore are required to be strong programmers in a variety of languages (especially Python). Previous ML or statistical research internship experience in finance, technology, or academia is strongly preferred.Working HereMan Systematic fosters a performance driven, meritocratic culture with a small company, no-attitude feel. It is flat structured, open, transparent, and collaborative, offering ample opportunity to grow and have enormous impact on what we do. We are actively engaged with the broader research and academic community, as well as renowned industry contributors.We’re fortunate enough to have a modern high-rise office in central Midtown conveniently located near Central Park and continually strive to make our environment a great place in which to work.We have annual away days and research off-sites for the whole team.We open-source some of our technology. See https://github.com/man-groupWe regularly talk at leading industry conferences, and tweet about relevant technology and how we’re using it. See @manquanttech and @ManGroup.Our Oxford lab is collocated with the Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance (https://bit.ly/36goTic) and the Machine Learning Research Group in Engineering Science, University of Oxford (https://bit.ly/2MSHDwy)

jobs.title: Engineering Co-Op: Spring 2027 at Safran Electrical & Power
jobs.description: Employer: Safran Electrical & Power - Safran Electrical & Power Expires: 11/11/2026 We're looking for students interested in working hands-on on real engineering projects. We offer Spring, Summer, and Fall rotations in a handful of areas (see below for more info). Our goal is to bridge the gap between classroom and real experience. Our hope is for students to feel like the work they're doing is valuable whilst challenging. Depending on a candidate's specialties and assigned area, roles require the following: Passion for mechanical, electrical, computer, or aerospace engineering, manufacturing, and technology. Strong analytical ability to solve problems and ability to learn quickly. Strong written & verbal communication skills to generate process instructions and reports. Ability to follow a structured project management process including document meeting minutes, action items, and monitor progress. Capability and tenacity for solving unique engineering problems. Ability to learn quickly and a desire to keep improving skills and to teach others when possible. Team player with a highly proactive and positive attitude with ability to work on own or in a team as needed. Hands-on skills. Demonstrated interest in building and testing. Regular, predictable attendance is required. Please note that estimated time for start/end dates are based on Spring 2027. Other semesters will have different dates. Want to know more about each of our Area Assignments? Let our managers tell you! Conversion Engineering: The Conversion Engineering Team is responsible for controller-generators and starter-generators (as well as converting the power they produce). We design and support multiple products with our current new product introduction (NPI) programs. The Mechanical Engineering Team designs the housings and assembly methods for our systems, ensuring they meet strict environmental and operational requirements. Their work is essential to delivering robust and reliable solutions for our aerospace applications. Embedded Systems Engineering: If you're curious about how hardware and software come together to power real-world systems and are eager to make an impact while learning from experienced engineers - join our Embedded Systems Engineering team. Industrialization Engineering: Industrialization is the perfect blend of design and manufacturing work. We have a mix of both in reviewing engineering drawings, discussing design features, developing solutions, mitigating design risks, managing prototype builds, building tooling, and implementing new products into production. We get the benefit of working with every department in the business and every day is different. If you want to have a mix of design work behind a desk and time on the production floor seeing designs you helped create come to life - then Industrialization is right for you! Manufacturing Engineering: As a Co-Op, you will work directly with our production team and design engineers to support the assembly and troubleshooting of aircrafts power-conversion units. We perform root-cause analysis on units that fail functional testing, remove roadblocks for our production team, diagnose defective parts, improve assembly processes, update work instructions, and initiate corrective actions. If you want hands-on experience on the shop floor and to improve efficiency while reducing waste - apply for Manufacturing Engineering. Production Support Engineering: Working in Production Support Engineering you will have the opportunity to work on real products and support day-to-day engineering activities that directly impact production, product reliability, and customer satisfaction. Responsibilities may include assisting with failure investigations, supporting resolution of production and supplier-related issues, evaluating nonconforming hardware, participating in repair and overhaul activities, reviewing engineering documentation, and contributing to engineering changes that improve product performance, manufacturability, and long-term supportability. Project Management: Everything starts with an idea, and project managers bring ideas into reality. From managing and executing plans, creative problem solving, and balancing the needs and expectations of a cross-functional team; project managers touch every aspect of the business and the world around us. With Project Management at Safran you will get real world understanding of how products and projects come to life, leveraging the strength of the team and how to manage risks and budget along the way. Quality Engineering: If you're looking to help ensure customer satisfaction and promote continual improvement of our products and processes, then the Quality Team may be for you. Our team is responsible for maintaining our Quality Management System (QMS), facilitating Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), and conducting internal quality audits. We promote continual improvement in the form of corrective actions and improvement projects. Rotating Machines Engineering: The mechanical design team within the Rotating Machines Department excels in engineering robust and high-performance aircraft rotating machinery. This includes generators and starter-generator systems. This group specializes in designing critical mechanical components such as rotors, stators, shafts, bearings, splines, and housings to ensure reliability and efficiency under demanding aerospace conditions. Supply Chain Engineering: Supply Chain is where ideas are transformed into finished products. We partner closely with suppliers to secure everything the business requires—from engineering components to the materials, equipment, and services that support daily operations. You'll gain firsthand experience in turning plans into reality by collaborating with suppliers, resolving challenges, and ensuring materials flow efficiently throughout the process. Systems/ Analysis Engineering: The System Integration & Performance Team develops, integrates, and validates aerospace electrical power systems by bringing together hardware, software, and control systems into a complete solution. Team members support system testing, performance analysis, troubleshooting, and certification activities to ensure products meet customer and regulatory requirements. Test Engineering: The Test Engineering Team specializes in test design, execution, and reporting for all power units. The team is composed of both test engineers and test equipment engineers. The test engineers handle the design, setup, execution, reporting of research and development testing, and qualification testing of new products and/or systems. Meanwhile, the test equipment engineering team design mechanical, electrical, and control equipment for the test lab to enable both production and new product testing to take place. Through Life Support Engineering: The Through Life Support Engineering team works on the problems that happen after designs enter production. The team investigates failures (both in the field and on the production line), solves production and supplier issues, supports repair and overhaul activity, evaluates nonconforming hardware, manages obsolescence, and develops design and drawing changes that keep products operating safely and reliably throughout their service life. For Co-Ops, it is a great opportunity to work on real hardware, see how engineering decisions affect the entire product lifecycle, and gain hands-on experience through a wide variety of technical challenges compared to working on a piece of a long-term development program.

It consists of twelve Reserve Banks located around the country and the Board of Governors in Washington, D.C. The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta territory covers the Sixth Federal Reserve District, which includes Alabama, Florida, and Georgia, and portions of Louisiana, Mississippi, and Tennessee. jobs.description: Employer: ANS Expires: 11/13/2026 Lab Engineer (Intern)Oklahoma City, OKLab – Intern - Oklahoma City, OK /Internship /On-siteThe Lab Engineer (Intern) plays a crucial role in advancing ANS's geotechnical engineering initiatives by conducting soil testing within our in-house geotechnical lab. jobs.description: Employer: 7-Eleven Inc Expires: 11/13/2026 Job DescriptionWe Began As An Original. We Remain An Original At The Top Of The Convenience Industry. Our company invented the concept of convenience retailing. But we didn’t stop there. 7-Eleven® has captured the world with a proven willingness and ability to innovate. We were the first company in America to offer fresh-brewed to-go coffee. More than six million of our Slurpee® beverages have been sipped since 1966. And, to continuously stay ahead of the curve, we introduce more than 2,500+ new products each year. With over 86,000 global locations, 7-Eleven Inc. is the world’s largest operator, franchiser and licensor of convenience stores and is also one of the nation’s largest independent gasoline retailers. The company continues to achieve operational accolades, win awards in franchising and drive innovation in retail in the mission to make life a little easier for our guests by being where they need us, when they need us. About these Opportunities: 7-Eleven Inc. has several opportunities for Summer Internships. Each internship opportunity will occur during the summer months, (11 weeks), focused on a specific functional area, and will provide the candidate with a depth experience within the area, culminating in a project presentation to functional leaders. Each intern will work closely with a coach who will meet regularly to discuss project progress, provide direction and ongoing feedback. In addition, each intern will attend a lunch series which will provide a cross-functional view into the organization and give the interns exposure to senior leadership. The interns will also have the experience of touring a store and learning about our distribution systems. In this role, the individual will act as a vital link between IT, Store Operations and various Store Support Center departments to improve and simplify stores processes and systems. Serves as RIS expert and escalation point for Operations Management for resolution of store RIS issues, 7hub, Store IA and related tools used to support the operations team.
